title: Near Earth, air resistance means a real drop is not pure freefall
summary: OpenStax says that near Earth a falling object is never truly in freefall, because air always pushes up a little.
body: After defining freefall as weight alone, OpenStax Physics says objects falling toward Earth are never truly in freefall. There is always some upward force from air resistance, and also a buoyancy force from the air. A NASA page on the Apollo 15 vacuum drop is the contrasting case, and it is not restated here. This card is the textbook's limit on drops in air. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020.
